A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RealUID research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renamed material.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR-10 generation experiments, coefficient ablations, convergence curves, fine-tuning results, and inference measurements in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: V2 retains original CIFAR-10 experiments and adds CelebA results and direct diffusion-model experiments in Appendices D.3 and A.3.

M1.justification: The core objectives and architecture remain intact. Algorithm 1 corrects the update condition from n % K to n % (K+1), aligning the written procedure with the already stated K fake-model updates per generator update. This establishes a pseudocode correction, not that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: V1 restricts image experiments to conditional and unconditional CIFAR-10 at 32×32 resolution. V2 retains these tasks and adds CelebA face generation at 64×64, substantially broadening the represented image domain. The additional SiD experiments reuse CIFAR-10.

E2.justification: V2 adds sCD, sCT, IMM, MeanFlow, and FACM to the unconditional comparison in Table 3. It also adds direct SiD-versus-RealSiD comparisons in Appendix A.3 and includes GAN methods in the fine-tuning comparison in Table 6, which previously evaluated only RealUID.

E3.justification: Reported CIFAR-10 settings change from AdamW to Adam, and unconditional teacher provenance changes from an authors-trained teacher to an existing checkpoint. Coefficient searches and fine-tuning configurations are revised, and GAN fine-tuning is added. New CelebA protocols use batch size 64 and 800,000/1,600,000 iterations. The PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 expands coefficient and fine-tuning sensitivity studies, adds a corrupted-teacher Gaussian case study in Figure 4, and tests real-data incorporation into SiD at alpha_SiD=0.5 and 1.2 in Figure 5. These investigate teacher errors and transfer of coefficient recommendations beyond the original flow-model experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independent FID evaluation runs with empirical variance below 0.01 and average inference timing over 10,000 iterations. V2 does not introduce seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Best reported CIFAR-10 RealUID FIDs change from 2.03/1.91 to 1.98/1.87 under revised coefficient and fine-tuning configurations, rather than identical settings. V2 adds fine-tuned GAN results of 2.10/1.88. New CelebA results in Table 8 are 0.96 for UID, 0.87 for UID+GAN, and 0.89 for RealUID; Figure 5 adds SiD convergence and instability findings.

T1.justification: The original UID and RealUID theorems are retained, but Appendix A.1.4 newly derives the objective for corrupted teachers and analyzes possible error correction under additional assumptions. Appendix A.2 extends coefficient-domain analysis, including conditions yielding unbounded objectives. Moving and algebraically rewriting the existing Lemma 2 is not itself new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion retain the central contributions: unifying matching-model distillation and incorporating real data without additional GAN losses or discriminators. The claimed framework coverage and exclusion of DMD from UID remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds a conditional explanation of teacher-error correction and emphasizes beta/alpha when interpreting real-data influence. Unlike v1's recommendation of alpha_SiD in [1,1.2], v2 discusses degradation or instability at 1.2 and limits theoretically justified guidance to 0.5. It also explains fine-tuning as requiring stronger real-data influence.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code release; v2 reports available code and checkpoints and supplies access links. It adds implementation information about reversed codebase time conventions, dropout, adversarial-loss time ranges, teacher provenance, CelebA training, and EMA choices. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although linked resources were not independently checked.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting newer comparators, CelebA, Adam, and EMA, and removes the AdamW reference. The central positioning relative to FGM, SiD, IBMD, inverse optimization, and DMD remains stable. Tong et al. changes from preprint to publication metadata for the same work.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are retained, with explanatory rewrites and terminology refinements. V2 moves Lemma 2 into Section 3.4, consolidates experimental Appendices D–E into organized Appendix D subsections, and adds publication, broader-impact, and LLM-use text.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 6 are substantially restructured around beta/alpha, with expanded grids, GAN fine-tuning blocks, and revised highlighting. Figure 2 is redrawn; Figures 4–6 and CelebA sample grids are added. CIFAR-10 grids use larger thumbnails, while the unchanged inference table moves into Appendix D.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's narrow empirical validation through CelebA and diffusion-model experiments, extends fine-tuning controls to GAN comparators, and reports a meaningful failure case for heuristic SiD. Expanded implementation and access information also improves reproducibility. These gains improve the paper beyond its small FID changes. The teacher-error argument remains conditional, and uncertainty reporting is unchanged, but these limitations do not outweigh the stronger validation and clearer applicability boundaries.
